paper.title: Prior-Free Competitive Ratios for Improving Bandits: Scale, Curvature and Horizon Are Free, but Not Jointly Under Noise

settings.name_in_paper: Improving multi-armed bandits (noiseless), known horizon, scale-oblivious
unmapped: Objective is the competitive ratio OPT_T / E[ALG_T] against the best single arm, not regret
Rewards are deterministic nondecreasing discretely concave curves f_i of the arm's own pull count, f_i(0)=0, fixed by an oblivious adversary
Algorithm does not know the scale m = f_*(T) nor the envelope exponent beta
settings.definition_quote: An instance consists of $k$ arms; arm $i$ has a reward function $f_i:\{0,1,\dots,T\}\to\R_{\ge0}$ with $f_i(0)=0$, nondecreasing, and with \emph{diminishing returns} ... Pulling arm $i$ for the $t$-th time yields $f_i(t)$ ... An algorithm has \emph{competitive ratio} $\rho$ if $\OPT_T\le\rho\,\E[\ALG_T]$ on every instance

settings.name_in_paper: Improving multi-armed bandits (noiseless), unknown horizon (anytime), scale-oblivious
unmapped: Objective is the competitive ratio OPT_T / E[ALG_T] against the best single arm
Rewards are deterministic nondecreasing discretely concave curves of the arm's pull count
Algorithm reads only k (not T, m, beta)
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm is \emph{scale-oblivious} if it does not read $m$ ..., \emph{$\beta$-oblivious} if it does not read $\beta$ ..., and \emph{anytime} if it does not read $T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits, known envelope exponent beta, unknown scale, known horizon
unmapped: Competitive-ratio objective
Learner knows the envelope exponent beta (comparator satisfies f(t) >= f(T)(t/T)^beta)
Deterministic concave improving reward curves
settings.definition_quote: for $\beta\in(0,1]$ we say that arm $i$ satisfies $\LE(\beta)$ if the inequality $f_i(t)\ge f_i(T)\,(t/T)^\beta$ holds for all $t\le T$.

unmapped: Competitive-ratio objective

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits with multiplicative noise, known horizon
unmapped: Observed/earned reward hat f_i(t) in [(1-eps)f_i(t),(1+eps)f_i(t)], fixed in advance by oblivious adversary (multiplicative adversarial noise)
Competitive-ratio objective against R (uncorrupted) or hat R
Algorithm does not know eps, m or beta
settings.definition_quote: when we pull an arm, instead of getting the exact value of $f_i(t_i)$, we get a reward value $\hat f_i(t_i)\in[(1-\varepsilon)f_i(t_i),(1+\varepsilon)f_i(t_i)]$; the algorithm observes and earns $\hat f$. The noisy values are fixed by the oblivious adversary before the run

algorithms.name: SRMP^cf (blocked confidence-key SRMP)
requires_knowledge_of: upper bound on noise level eps

algorithms.name: Uniform mixture of APC, phased NPA and anytime SRMP

conditions: reward curves nondecreasing, discretely concave, f(0)=0

source.label: thm:TA
source.quote: Let $k\ge2$, $T\ge2\lfloor\sqrt k\rfloor$, $s=\lfloor\sqrt k\rfloor$, $\tau=\lfloor T/(2s)\rfloor$. Then $\PC(s,\tau)$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{s}{8k}R\ge\frac{R}{16\sqrt k}$, and in fact $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{R}{4\sqrt3\,\sqrt k}$. For $k=1$ the ratio is $1$. The algorithm uses no information about $m$.

results.notes: Bound is on the competitive ratio OPT_T/E[ALG_T]; quantity 'other'. Also states the weaker ratio 16 sqrt(k).

tuning: tau = floor(T/(2s)); T=1: uniform random arm

source.label: thm:allT
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, the minimax ratio of scale-oblivious algorithms satisfies $\frac14\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)\le\rho(k,T)\le24\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)$.

results.notes: Competitive ratio upper bound via PC with truncated parameters.

source.label: thm:allT
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, the minimax ratio of scale-oblivious algorithms satisfies $\frac14\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)\le\rho(k,T)\le24\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)$.

results.notes: Lower bound on minimax competitive ratio, from Corollary 3.7.

conditions: hard instances: one linear arm g(t)=t/T, others truncated at d=floor(T/sqrt(k))

source.label: cor:L4
source.quote: For every randomized algorithm there is an instance on which its competitive ratio is at least (a) $\sqrt k/3$, for all $k,T\ge1$ (take $g(t)=t/T$, $d=\lfloor T/\sqrt k\rfloor$); and (b) $k/T$

results.notes: Restates with integer bookkeeping the BR25 lower bound; paper presents as its own corollary.

conditions: hard instance: one linear arm and k-1 zero arms

source.label: cor:L4
source.quote: (b) $k/T$ (take $g(t)=t/T$, $d=0$: one linear arm and $k-1$ arms identically zero).

results.notes: Competitive-ratio lower bound.

source.label: thm:anytime
source.quote: Let $s=\lfloor\sqrt k\rfloor$ and run phases of lengths $L_j=2s\cdot2^j$, ... The algorithm reads only $k$, and for every $T\ge2s$, $\E[\ALG_T]\ge R/(256\sqrt k)$.

results.notes: Competitive ratio.

source.label: thm:anytimeAll
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, $\APC$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{R}{1536\,(\sqrt k+k/T)}$.

results.notes: Competitive ratio.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1]: comparator satisfies f(t) >= f(T)(t/T)^beta

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: Let $\beta\in(0,1]$ be known and suppose the comparator arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$. For $k\ge2$, $T\ge2\lceil K_\beta\rceil$, $s=\lceil K_\beta\rceil$, $\tau=\lfloor T/(2s)\rfloor$, $\PC(s,\tau)$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge R/(16k^{\gamma})$.

results.notes: gamma = beta/(1+beta). Competitive ratio.

conditions: all arms satisfy LE(beta) with envelope exponent exactly beta

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: for every $k\ge2$ and $T\ge2$ there is an explicit distribution over instances, all of whose arms satisfy $\LE(\beta)$ and whose envelope exponent equals $\beta$, on which \emph{every} (possibly randomized) algorithm has expected reward at most $(\beta+2)k^{-\gamma}\OPT_T$; hence ... $\rho_\beta(k,T)\ge k^\gamma/(\beta+2)$

results.notes: Holds even if beta (and scale) are known. Variant of BGRS26 Thm 3.6.

conditions: instances in I_beta (an optimal arm satisfies LE(beta))

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: for all $T\ge1$, $\frac{k^\gamma+k/T}{\beta+3}\le\rho_\beta(k,T)\le24(k^\gamma+k/T)$;

results.notes: Class-wise minimax lower bound.

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: for all $T\ge1$, $\frac{k^\gamma+k/T}{\beta+3}\le\rho_\beta(k,T)\le24(k^\gamma+k/T)$;

results.notes: Uses PC with truncated beta-tuned parameters.

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: with $T$ unknown: for $k\ge2$ and $s=\lceil K_\beta\rceil$, independent $\PC$ phases of lengths $2s\cdot2^j$ ($j=0,1,\dots$) without resetting pull counts give $\E[\ALG_T]\ge R/(128k^\gamma)$ for every $T\ge2s$

results.notes: Competitive ratio.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of the optimal arm (not known to the algorithm)

source.label: thm:TG
source.quote: Let $k\ge2$, $\beta\in(0,1]$, $T\ge16k$, and suppose the optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$. Then $\RMP(T)$, which reads neither $m$ nor $\beta$, satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{3}{256}\,R\,k^{-\beta/(1+\beta)}$.

results.notes: Holds simultaneously for all beta. Also gives a depth-oracle bound E/R >= (3/1024) min{f_*(d)/m, T/(kd)} not recorded separately.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of the optimal arm

source.label: thm:TGp
source.quote: Run $\RMP(H_j)$ in phases $H_j=16k\cdot2^j$ with fresh weights, without resetting the true pull counts. The algorithm reads only $k$, and for every $\beta\in(0,1]$, every instance whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, and every $T\ge16k$, $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{3}{4096}Rq_\beta$.

results.notes: q_beta = K^{-beta/(1+beta)}.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of the optimal arm

source.label: thm:W46
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, all $\beta\in(0,1]$ and all instances whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, $\SRMP(k,T)$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{R}{c_{\mathrm{SR}}}\min\Big\{k^{-\beta/(1+\beta)},\ \frac Tk\Big\},\qquad c_{\mathrm{SR}}:=2^{13}=8192$.

results.notes: Ratio = 1/min = Max. Paper also states ratio <= 8192(k^gamma + k/T); lower bound part restates Thm 3.13(ii).

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of the optimal arm

source.label: thm:W47
source.quote: Run $\SRMP$ in phases of lengths $1,2,4,\dots$, each with fresh randomness ... The algorithm reads only $k$, and for every $T\ge1$, $\E[\ALG_T]\ge2^{-19}\,R\,Q_\beta(k,T)$.

results.notes: Q_beta = min{K^{-gamma}, T/K}.

symbols.eps_noise: multiplicative noise level epsilon (not known to the algorithm)

source.label: thm:H1
source.quote: Let $\PC$ commit to the arm with the largest observed probe value. For every instance and admissible $(s,\tau)$, $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{b}\,R\,\min\{...\}$ ... each algorithm of Section~\ref{sec:scale} keeps its guarantee up to the factor $a^2/b$ ... $\PC$, $T$ known (Thm.~\ref{thm:TA}) & $16\sqrt k$

results.notes: a=1-eps, b=1+eps. Against hat R multiply by an extra b.

source.label: thm:H1
source.quote: $\PC$, truncated parameters (Thm.~\ref{thm:allT}) & $24(\sqrt k+k/T)$ & all $T\ge1$ ... the noisy minimax ratio of scale-oblivious algorithms is $\Theta(\sqrt k+k/T)$ at every horizon

results.notes: Table row of Theorem 5.1.

source.label: thm:H1
source.quote: $\APC$, $T$ unknown (Thm.~\ref{thm:anytimeAll}) & $1536(\sqrt k+k/T)$ & all $T\ge1$

results.notes: Table row of Theorem 5.1.

source.label: thm:H1
source.quote: doubling $\PC$, $T$ unknown (Thm.~\ref{thm:anytime}) & $256\sqrt k$ & $T\ge2\lfloor\sqrt k\rfloor$

results.notes: Table row; known-beta rows (16/q_beta, 256/q_beta) not recorded separately.

source.label: thm:H2U
source.quote: For every $\beta\in(0,1]$, every instance whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, and $T\ge16k$, $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{64b}\,\frac{R\,q_\beta}{\PhiK(k)}\ge\frac{a^2}{64b^2}\,\frac{\hat R\,q_\beta}{\PhiK(k)}$. With $T$ unknown ... the constant becomes $1024$.

results.notes: Phi(k)=sqrt((1+ln k)/ln(e+ln k)). Algorithm reads neither m, beta nor eps.

source.label: thm:H2U
source.quote: With $T$ unknown (phases $16k\cdot2^j$, conditioning on history as in Lemma~\ref{lem:G4}) the constant becomes $1024$.

results.notes: Interpreted as replacing 64 by 1024 in the R-based bound.

conditions: ratio measured against noisy benchmark hat R
beta and instance chosen after the algorithm

source.label: thm:H2L
source.quote: For every $k\ge k_0(\varepsilon)$ and every algorithm that does not read $m$ or $\beta$ (it may read $T$ and $\varepsilon$), there exist $\beta\in(0,1]$, an instance whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, and a fixed in-band noise table such that $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\le\frac{8192}{\varepsilon\,\PhiK(k)}\,\hat R\,q_\beta$.

results.notes: Lower bound on competitive ratio hat R/E[hat ALG]; algorithm class: algorithms not reading m or beta. Gives phi_eps(k) = Theta_eps(sqrt(log k/log log k)).

source.label: thm:RET
source.quote: In particular, when the scale of a cumulatively optimal arm is known --- take $H=T$ and $\mu=m=f_\ast(T)$ ... we get $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac a{2048b}Rq_\beta$ simultaneously for every such $\beta$, without reading $\beta$ or $\varepsilon$

results.notes: Main statement: E >= a/(2048 b) mu H q_beta.

conditions: scale advice m tied to the evaluation horizon

source.label: thm:RET
source.quote: If in addition $T$ is unknown, running $\RET(H_j,\mu)$ in phases $H_j=16k\cdot2^j$ with the advice $\mu=m/4$ gives $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac a{32768\,b}Rq_\beta$ for every $T\ge16k$, in the advice model

results.notes: Advice model: single advice for the evaluation horizon.

symbols.c_epsbar: (1+epsbar)/(1-epsbar) - (1-epsbar)/(1+epsbar) for the supplied noise upper bound epsbar in [0,1/2]

source.label: prop:W48
source.quote: There is an algorithm $\SRMPc$ ... which reads $k$, $T$ and any valid upper bound $\bar\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon$ ... and which satisfies, for all integers $k,T\ge1$, every $\beta\in(0,1]$ and every instance whose comparator satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{65536\,b\,D(k,T,\bar\varepsilon)}\,R\,Q_\beta(k,T)$.

results.notes: Consequence: limsup as eps->0 of ratio <= 65536 for fixed k.

source.label: cor:mixture
source.quote: It reads none of $m,\beta,T,\varepsilon$, and $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{b}\cdot\frac{R}{4608(\sqrt k+k/T)}\ (\text{all }T\ge1)$

results.notes: Mixture algorithm.

source.label: cor:mixture
source.quote: $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{3072\,b}\cdot\frac{R\,q_\beta}{\PhiK(k)}\quad(T\ge16k)$, and, when $\varepsilon=0$, also $\E[\ALG_T]\ge R\,Q_\beta(k,T)/(3\cdot2^{19})$

results.notes: Noiseless third guarantee 3*2^19 Max(K^gamma, K/T) not recorded separately.
